title: Lamb Tagine with Prunes, Apricots and Almonds
summary: Lamb shoulder braises slowly with ginger, turmeric, cinnamon and saffron until meltingly tender, then is served with honeyed prunes and apricots and crunchy toasted almonds.
equipment: large heavy casserole (Dutch oven, 5-6 litres) with tight lid, or a tagine with a heat diffuser

ingredients.item: boneless lamb shoulder, trimmed of excess fat, cut into 4 cm pieces
fine sea salt or table salt
saffron threads (about 20), crumbled into 2 tbsp hot water
fresh coriander, stalks tied in a bunch, leaves chopped for serving

steps.title: Prepare the lamb
steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C (fan 140°C) and season the lamb with the tagine salt and pepper. Seasoning before browning lets the salt start drawing flavour into the surface of the meat.

steps.title: Brown in batches
steps.text: Heat the oil in the casserole over medium-high heat and brown the lamb in 2-3 batches, 6-8 min each, without crowding the pan. Each piece should be well coloured on several sides before you lift it out. Crowding traps steam, so the meat would turn grey instead of browning.

steps.title: Build the spiced base
steps.text: With the heat lowered to medium, cook the onions for 8-10 min until soft and golden. Stir in the garlic, fresh and ground ginger, turmeric, coriander, ground cinnamon and the cinnamon stick for 1 min until fragrant. Spices release their aromatic oils when briefly fried in fat.

steps.title: Slow braise
steps.text: Return the lamb and its juices, then add the saffron and its water, the 500 ml water and the coriander stalks, scraping up the browned bits. Bring to a simmer, cover tightly and braise in the oven for 2 h-2 h 30 min, stirring once or twice. The lamb is ready when it yields easily to a spoon, as long gentle heat melts its connective tissue.

steps.title: Simmer the fruit
steps.text: Meanwhile, simmer the prunes, apricots, honey, cinnamon and 150 ml water in the small saucepan for 10-12 min. Stop when the fruit looks plump and the liquid has turned into a glossy syrup.

steps.title: Toast the almonds
steps.text: Fry the almonds in the oil in the small pan over medium-low heat for 4-5 min until golden, adding the sesame seeds for the final minute. Moderate heat toasts the nuts right through without scorching the outside.

steps.title: Finish the sauce
steps.text: Lift out the coriander stalks and cinnamon stick. If the sauce looks thin, simmer it uncovered on the hob for 5-10 min until it coats the meat; evaporation concentrates both flavour and body.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Spoon the lamb into a warm dish, top with the fruit and its syrup, and scatter over the almonds, sesame seeds and chopped coriander leaves. Offer bread or couscous alongside to soak up the sauce.

tips: A common mistake is rushing the browning; well-coloured lamb gives the sauce much of its depth, so work in batches.
Cook the fruit separately so it stays whole and glossy instead of dissolving into the stew.
Watch the almonds closely in the last minute, as they go from golden to burnt very quickly.
The tagine tastes even better the next day, so it is ideal for cooking ahead.
storage: Cool within 2 hours and refrigerate for up to 3 days, or freeze the lamb and sauce for up to 3 months. Reheat until piping hot (74°C) and add freshly warmed fruit and almonds to serve.
